note: From the OpenStreetMap export (the corridor's tracks and platforms, 8 October 2026), at real scale across the line like the tracks: bays 1 to 12 run back from the buffer stops at about u = 40, platform 5 (the stopper, turning round) on the corridor, the rest laid parallel to it as islands 2/3, 4/5, 6/7, 8/9 and the single platforms 1, 10, 11 and 12, the four Longsight lines closing up into platform 5's road and the bays' lead, bays 6 to 12 leaving the down slow westwards in one lead from u = -880, and the two Hope Valley lines (the Marple trains') into 3 and 2, with 4 leaving the first westwards and 1 the second eastwards (re-laid from OpenStreetMap 14 October 2026; network.json's layout note). The bays run parallel under the shed and their tracks fan into the throat beyond the platform ends; how far each platform splays the photos can't settle (geograph 6532170 and 6532172, aerial 2020, are too blurred), so the platforms stay parallel. Trains stop 35 m short of the station's point so the longest unit clears the buffers. Positive v is east (London Road side). Photos: the great glazed arched train shed over the bays, and canopies on columns along the platforms that run out beyond it. It starts as a halt: a strip of the island along platform 5 with lamps. The concourse (with room for barriers and the food hall), then the train shed and the other bays, build it up; the tracks are scenery. A departure board on platform 5 and over the concourse end facing the platforms; the cycle racks outside the concourse with it (no dedicated cycle hub shows in the photos, only racks by the London Road entrance, geograph 7974366 2025). Photos (geograph 5158151, 6416982, 6882401 and 7158891 Gerald England 2016-22, 8399536 to 8399546 DS Pugh 2026, 2930696 2010, 4926749 Stephen Craven 2016, 5158023 2016, 7305361 2022, 2755385 Stephen Richards 2011, 7922589 Mike Parker 2024, 8195813 2025, 3036447 2012, 3593280 2013, 8257910 and 8257927 2026, 5693935 2017, 6578168 2020): platforms 13 and 14 are a through island on the viaduct south-west of the shed (the -v side), drawn as scenery since the line doesn't run through them until phase 6: about 250 m long, brick parapets, a canopy over the middle third only, a glazed waiting room, and a lounge over the island reached by the high-level walkway from the shed (the travelators along 11 and 12 rise to it). Their tracks run on along the bays' lead beyond bay 12 and out to them at no more than 1 in 6. Since 13 and 14 are on the -v side, the real platform 1 is on the +v side and the numbers in this note run the other way from the real ones (handed on). Gateway House is the S-shaped office slab on the north-east side of Station Approach, about 150 m long and nine storeys (30 m) of silver bands and ribbon glazing, as scenery. The multi-storey car park is clad in weathering steel, five or six decks and over 100 m long, north-east of the shed across Sheffield Street on Boad Street, at its real outline (OpenStreetMap, 14 October 2026), the decks for sale on its roof. The concourse front is a tall glass wall with a pitched canopy over the forecourt (with the concourse). Across the line at real scale since 13 October 2026 (it was 1.25 times).
